## OverviewThe society, economy, and culture of the mortal races are defined by a single overarching reality: **survival through unity**. Two centuries after the founding of the Last Stand, the mortal races have built a civilization unlike any before it — one born of necessity, shaped by shared struggle, and defined by the ongoing reconquering of their ancestral lands from the monster hordes.Three capital cities — Skywatch, Emberforge, and Weaveheart — form the political, economic, and cultural heart of this civilization. The recovered territories to the south and east provide resources, trade, and farmland. The western frontier is where the war for survival continues. And across it all, the presence of the divine pantheon — and the truth the gods hide — casts a long shadow.---
## Governance & Political Structure
> **Note:** The political structure of the mortal races is still young and settling. The reconquering has happened in phases over the past ~200 years — some territories have been held for generations, others reclaimed within living memory. As a result, governance varies widely between settlements and regions. What follows is the framework at the highest level, with local details left for when specific settlements are developed.
#
## The Council Accord (The Three Kings)The three capital cities are each ruled by a **King**, and together the three kings form the **Council Accord** — the closest thing mortal civilization has to a central authority. The Accord has no fixed schedule; the kings gather frequently by tradition, and any one of them may invoke a formal council when matters affecting all three cities arise.This structure exists by design:
- **No single point of failure** — if one city falls, the others continue
- **Specialization** — each city focuses on its strengths (scouting, forging, magic)
- **Shared threat** — the monster invasion forces cooperation; no city can survive aloneHowever, the system is far from rigid. Each king governs their city differently, reflecting the unique circumstances and history of their capital. Beneath each king, advisory bodies — councils, circles, conclaves, guilds, or clans — handle the day-to-day administration of their domains.
#
## The Three Kings & Their Governments#
#
## Skywatch — The King and the Council of EyesSkywatch's king rules with the counsel of the **Council of Eyes**, a body of the most accomplished scouts, rangers, and strategists. Leadership at the council level is meritocratic — seats are earned through proven service and expertise. Skywatch's rule is practical, direct, and focused on intelligence gathering, vigilance, and military readiness. *(Further detail on Skywatch's internal power dynamics to be defined when the city is developed.)*#
#
## Emberforge — The King and the Forgemaster's CircleEmberforge's king rules with the counsel of the **Forgemaster's Circle**, representing the most powerful smithing guilds, engineering houses, and industrial clans. Emberforge's internal politics are shaped by production output, resource control, and the influence of its major craft families. *(Further detail on Emberforge's internal power dynamics to be defined when the city is developed.)*#
#
## Weaveheart — The King and the Arcane ConclaveWeaveheart's king rules with the counsel of the **Arcane Conclave**, an assembly of the most powerful wizards, scholars, and arcane researchers. Weaveheart is a magocracy in practice — knowledge of the weave translates directly into political influence. The Conclave oversees magical research, education, and the maintenance of the magical barrier. *(Further detail on Weaveheart's internal power dynamics to be defined when the city is developed.)*
#
## The Young & Fluid Nature of PowerBecause the reconquering is ongoing and the territories were reclaimed in stages, the political landscape is diverse and still crystallizing:
- **In frontier settlements and recently-reclaimed zones**, power tends to follow **strength and survival** — a clan with the most capable fighters, the shrewdest leader, or the deepest knowledge of the land may hold sway regardless of formal titles.
- **In long-secured heartland settlements**, more traditional power structures have had time to emerge — wealthy families, established guilds, and inherited influence shape local governance.
- **The three capitals** sit between these extremes: old enough to have traditions, young enough to still be defining them.This diversity means that a noble title in one settlement may carry no weight in another, and the relationship between any two settlements is shaped as much by the personality of their leaders as by formal political structures.
#
## The Militarized SocietyAll three capitals operate under a **wartime footing**. Every able-bodied citizen is expected to contribute to the reconquering effort:
- Military service (active duty, militia, or reserve)
- Industrial production (forging weapons, crafting armor, producing supplies)
- Logistical support (farming, transport, construction)
- Arcane contribution (enchanting, barrier maintenance, research)Conscription is rare — the shared threat and cultural pride in the reconquering mean that most citizens volunteer. Those who serve gain status, land grants, and preferential treatment in housing and trade.
#
## The Survival Code & Local Law#
#
## The Survival Code (Foundation Law)The **Survival Code** is the foundational legal framework agreed upon across all reconquered territories. It is deliberately short and broad — a set of principles rather than a detailed legal system — designed to be adopted anywhere without conflict with local customs.**The Articles of the Survival Code:**
1. **The Article of Life** — No murder. The killing of a mortal by another mortal is forbidden except in self-defense, in defense of others, or under lawful military command.
2. **The Article of Supply** — No theft, hoarding, or sabotage of military supplies, food reserves, or materials critical to the war effort.
3. **The Article of Allegiance** — No treason. Aiding monsters, enemy forces, or knowingly undermining the reconquering is the highest crime.
4. **The Article of the Barrier** — No sabotage or deliberate destabilization of the magical barrier or any defensive ward protecting a settlement.
5. **The Article of Truth** — No false accusations under the Code. Those who knowingly levy false charges face the penalty that would have been applied to the accused.**Penalties under the Code:**
| Violation 
| Typical Penalty 
|
|-----------
|-----------------
|
| Murder (unlawful) 
| Exile beyond the barrier, or execution 
|
| Theft of supplies 
| Labor service (length depends on severity) 
|
| Treason 
| Execution 
|
| Barrier sabotage 
| Execution 
|
| False accusation 
| Same penalty as the false charge 
|Exile beyond the barrier is considered a death sentence in all but the most exceptional circumstances.#
#
## Local Ordinances & CustomBeyond the Survival Code, each settlement governs itself as it sees fit. This creates a patchwork of local laws and customs:
- **Weaveheart** strictly regulates dangerous magical experimentation and the trade of arcane reagents
- **Emberforge** controls mining claims, resource extraction, and guild membership requirements
- **Skywatch** enforces strict protocols around information sharing and scouting intelligence
- **Frontier settlements** often operate under martial law, with the local commander holding absolute authority
- **Long-established heartland towns** may have developed complex property laws, trade regulations, and inheritance customsWhere local law conflicts with the Survival Code, the Code takes precedence — but disputes over interpretation are common and often require mediation by a neutral third party or, in extreme cases, referral to the Council Accord.#
#
## JudgmentLegal proceedings are handled locally, with no standardized judiciary across all territories:
- **In the capitals**, trials are typically conducted before a panel of respected citizens — guild leaders for trade disputes, veteran officers for military matters, mages for arcane violations
- **In smaller settlements**, the local leader or council serves as judge, often with input from elders
- **In frontier outposts**, the commanding officer holds summary authority, though serious violations of the Code are expected to be referred to a capital for formal judgment---
## Social Structure
#
## Respect & StandingRespect in mortal society is earned through **concrete contributions to the reconquering** — measured by the threats one has neutralized, the territory one has helped reclaim, and the communities one has protected. A farmer who feeds a garrison, a smith who equips a company, a mage who maintains the barrier, and an adventurer who clears a monster nest are all respected — but the measure of that respect scales with the directness and danger of the contribution.There is no rigid caste or formal ranking system. Rather, reputation is local and earned:
- **A renowned monster hunter** might be celebrated in one town and unknown in the next
- **A master smith** from Emberforge carries weight in any settlement that relies on their weapons
- **A wealthy merchant** who funds a settlement's defenses may command influence far beyond their formal title
#
## Authority
> *To be defined per settlement when locations are developed.*Who holds authority in any given place depends entirely on local circumstances. In some settlements, it is the person who invested the most resources into rebuilding. In others, it is the one who personally defends the walls. In yet others, a major capital may have appointed a governor regardless of local sentiment. Each settlement's power structure will be detailed when that location is created.
#
## The Guild SystemMost professions are organized into guilds, which provide training, representation, and a social safety net for their members. Major guilds include:
- **Smiths' & Crafters' Guild** (Emberforge) — the largest and most politically influential
- **Scouts' & Rangers' Guild** (Skywatch)
- **Mages' & Scholars' Guild** (Weaveheart)
- **Farmers' & Herders' Guild** — spread across the recovered territories
- **Merchants' & Traders' Guild** — controls sea trade and caravan routes
- **Miners' & Prospectors' Guild** — operates mining operations in the south and east
- **[Guild Name TBD] — The Adventurers' Guild** — a continent-wide organization that manages monster-hunting contracts, ruin delving, and frontier exploration. Its members are collectively known by a nickname still to be defined.
#
## Tensions of a Young CivilizationBecause the reconquering is recent and governance is still settling, friction is common:
- **Who really contributes?** — Local disputes arise over which clan, family, or individual is doing the most for a community. A group that clears monster nests may feel slighted when a wealthy merchant family (who funded the rebuilding) holds political power.
- **Authority without mandate** — A settlement's de facto protector may start enforcing laws, patrolling streets, or judging disputes without any formal judicial authority. This is frequently a source of tension, especially when the Survival Code is invoked or challenged.
- **Capital vs. frontier** — A governor appointed by one of the three kings may clash with local power structures that emerged organically during the reconquering. Whose authority is legitimate?
- **Old vs. new** — Pre-invasion bloodlines and noble names carry weight in some places but are meaningless in others, creating resentment on both sides.---
## Economy
#
## Currency — Fragments of the PrimordialAll precious metals — gold, silver, copper, and platinum — as well as gemstones, are **fragments of B's physical remains** from the Great Sacrifice. This is why these materials are rare, valuable, and inherently magical (many spells require costly components). **Nobody knows this.** It is one of the deepest cosmological secrets of the setting, and its revelation is intended to be a major campaign-defining moment.The standard currency system follows familiar denominations:
- **Copper Pieces (cp)** — everyday transactions
- **Silver Pieces (sp)** — standard wage and trade currency
- **Gold Pieces (gp)** — high-value trade, magic items, large transactions
- **Platinum Pieces (pp)** — extremely rare, used by major guilds and high-level commerce#
#
## The Mint — [Northeast Settlement Cluster, Name TBD]Currency is minted in a cluster of settlements in the **northeast** of the continent. This area consists of **one major settlement and three minor ones**, plus two smaller nearby settlements that assist in exporting the currency. This was the site of the royal mint before the monster invasion, and after the reconquering, production resumed here. It remains the **backbone of the continental economy**.This region also contains the **greatest known mines** for both precious metals and gemstones, making it the single most economically vital area in the recovered territories. *(Further detail on the northeast settlement cluster to be defined when locations are developed.)*
#
## Major Industries#
#
## Mining & ProspectingThe **northeast settlement cluster** is the heart of mining operations, producing the bulk of precious metals and gemstones that fuel the economy. Additional mines exist in the recovered south and east. Operations are managed by the Miners' & Prospectors' Guild with strict quotas and safety regulations.#
#
## Metalworking & Smithing**Emberforge** is the industrial heart of the mortal races. Its volcanic forges produce:
- Weapons and armor for the Last Stand military
- Tools for farming, construction, and mining
- Components for arcane research and enchantment
- Unique alloys made possible by volcanic heat and rare oresEmberforge's technology is the most advanced on the continent, and its weapons are considered the finest available.#
#
## Agriculture & The Fertile ForestsThe forests surrounding the three capitals — where the Last Stand was founded — are exceptionally nutrient-rich, producing abundant food. This fertility is not natural: below Skywatch and Weaveheart, extending to the side of Emberforge, lies a **massive cave of arcane-reactive crystals** that blankets the entire area where the forest grows on top. The crystals' ambient energy seeps into the soil, supercharging its productivity. *(This is a plot hook to be developed.)*Staple crops across the recovered territories include:
- Grains (wheat, barley, oats) in the temperate regions
- Rice, exotic fruits, and spices in the subtropical south
- Livestock (cattle, sheep, poultry) across both regionsFood security is a strategic priority — the granaries of the three capitals maintain enough reserves to survive a siege of several years.#
#
## Arcane Industry & The Thormvuld FamilyThe **Thormvuld** family — dwarven arcane engineers established in a one-shot before the campaign — are the most prominent and proficient magical item producers on the continent. They originate from the **northeast settlement cluster** and also own a **small settlement south of it**, dedicated to their workshops and foundries.**Weaveheart** also produces high-quality enchanted equipment and houses a prestigious **mage college** that trains new spellcasters and advances arcane research. However, the Thormvulds remain the premier producers of magical goods.#
#
## Monster Hunting IndustryThe continent-wide adventurers' guild (name TBD) is the primary controller of this industry. Settlements, caravans, and military outposts contract the guild to clear monster nests, eliminate threats, and reclaim dangerous sites. This is one of the largest economic sectors, as the reconquering effort relies on it for frontier expansion.#
#
## The Last Alliance MilitaryThe unified army of the three capitals functions as a major economic force in its own right. Beyond its direct military role, it contracts local mercenary companies for specific operations — reconquering a settlement, securing a resource outpost, or reinforcing a frontier position. These contracts inject significant coin into local economies.#
#
## Sea Trade & PortsA major settlement to the **southeast** — heavily fortified, coastal, and highly defensible — serves as one of the main sea trade hubs. Another port settlement to the **east** provides additional sea connections. Together, they form the backbone of maritime commerce.Major exports include:
- From the south: exotic fruits, spices, timber, rare herbs
- From the northeast: precious metals, gemstones, minted currency
- From Emberforge: weapons, armor, industrial goods
- From Weaveheart: enchanted items, magical components
#
## Trade Routes#
#
## The Eastern Sea RouteA series of ports along the eastern coast, connecting the southern ports to the heartlands. Ships carry goods north and south, stopping at waypoint towns. Safer than land travel and handles the bulk of bulk trade.#
#
## Crassian's Dust CircleAn overland trade circuit connecting all major settlements — the three capitals, the northeast settlement cluster, the southeastern port, and the eastern port. The circuit was named after the great cloud of dust that arose when it was completed, as large trade caravans from across the recovered territories began using it all at once, covering the land and skies for days.#
#
## The Frontier RoadA dangerous, partially reclaimed road extending west from the heartlands into contested territory. Used by military supply convoys and frontier settlers, always under heavy guard.
#
## Economic Challenges
- **Resource scarcity** — many mines and forests in the north and west remain under monster control, limiting access to certain resources
- **Trade disruption** — monster attacks on caravans and ships, while reduced, still occur
- **War economy inflation** — military production consumes resources that could otherwise go to civilian development
- **Black market** — a thriving underground trade in monster parts, illegal magical components, and contraband operates in the shadows, often connected to existing organizations---
## Culture & Daily Life
#
## The Last Stand IdentityThe mortal races of Kythoria share a **unified cultural identity** forged by two centuries of shared struggle. Differences between races persist in traditions, cuisine, and aesthetics, but the overarching identity is one of **survival, unity, and defiance**.#
#
## Core Cultural Values
- **Unity** — "Together we stand, divided we fall" is not a slogan but a lived truth. Racism and prejudice are socially unacceptable, though individual biases still exist.
- **Resilience** — hardship is expected and met with determination. Stoicism is admired; complaint is seen as weakness.
- **Contribution** — every citizen is expected to do their part. Laziness and freeloading are heavily stigmatized.
- **Curiosity** — the desire to understand the world, recover lost knowledge, and discover new ways to fight the monsters drives innovation.
- **Faith** — religion is central to daily life, though the true nature of the gods is unknown to all but a few.
#
## Religion & The ChurchesThe pantheon of ten gods dominates religious life. *(Note: The pantheon has been expanded to ten gods: Vorn (War & Conquest) and Tyra (Hunt & Nature) added.)* Each god has an established church with temples in all three capitals and smaller shrines throughout the recovered territories.#
#
## The Church HierarchyEach god's church is organized independently, with its own priesthood, rituals, and sacred texts. The churches cooperate through the **Ecumenical Council**, a body that mediates disputes between faiths and coordinates major religious festivals.#
#

## The Manufactured Divine ConflictThe gods maintain an elaborate pantheon conflict — rivalries, alliances, and divine vendettas that their churches faithfully reproduce. The specific mapping of which gods are allied and which are opposed is **still to be defined**. What is known is that these conflicts are **manufactured** by the gods themselves to deepen faith and devotion. The common worshipper believes them to be real divine politics. Most priests believe them too. Only a handful of the highest-ranking clergy suspect the truth.#
#
## Daily Religious PracticeMost citizens offer a brief prayer at least once a day — typically at a small household shrine or at a neighborhood temple. The gods most commonly prayed to are:
- **Light and Life** — for healing, protection of family, good harvests
- **Forge and Arcana** — for success in craft, safe passage through the barrier
- **Wealth and Fortune** — for luck in trade and prospecting
#
## The Calendar & FestivalsA custom calendar system is in use:
- **10 months**, each named after a god in the order of the creation story
- **2 weeks per month** (20 days per month = 200 days per year)
- **10 days per week**: Wildtide, Lawrest, Duskfall, Life-dawn, Fangrest, Gravefall, Sparktide, Cointide, Warmorn, Shadowrest *(work/rest pattern: 4 work, 2 rest, 3 work, 1 rest)*The first day of the year is always **Wildtide** — the first day of Kaelthor, matching the beginning of creation. Each week follows a pattern of 4 workdays, 2 rest days, 3 workdays, and 1 rest day.#
#

## The Day of Silence

A solemn observance on the last day of the year (Shadowrest of the 2nd week of Lolth, day 200) — no work is done, no magic is cast, and citizens observe a day of quiet reflection to **honor the dead and the fallen** in the monster invasion and the reconquering. This is a secular tradition, not a religious one, born from the idea that even in a world of constant war, one day of peace and remembrance is sacred.
#
## Education & Knowledge#
#
## Formal EducationThe Last Stand operates a system of **public academies** in all three cities, funded by guild taxes:
- **Basic education** (ages 6-12): Reading, writing, arithmetic, basic history of the Last Stand, physical training
- **Apprenticeship** (ages 12-18): Specialized training in a guild trade or military service
- **Higher learning** (select individuals): Admission to the **Weaveheart Academy of Arcane Arts** (for mages) or the **Skywatch War College** (for officers and strategists)#
#
## Libraries & ArchivesEach capital maintains a major library:
- **Weaveheart's Grand Athenaeum** — the largest collection of arcane texts, historical records, and pre-invasion literature
- **Skywatch's Cartography Hall** — maps, scouting reports, intelligence archives
- **Emberforge's Engineering Archives** — schematics, metallurgical treatises, architectural plansLibraries are public but access to restricted sections requires guild membership or military clearance.#
#
## Lost KnowledgeThe monster invasion destroyed an immense amount of pre-invasion knowledge. Scholars estimate that **over 70% of pre-invasion written records were lost**. The recovery and preservation of ancient texts is a respected profession, and ruin-delving adventurers are frequently hired to retrieve books, scrolls, and tablets from monster-occupied sites.
#
## Arts & EntertainmentDespite the war footing, the mortal races have maintained a vibrant cultural life — perhaps as an act of defiance against the darkness.#
#
## Music & Performance
- **Bards** are highly respected as keepers of history, morale-boosters, and spies
- **The Skywatch Chorus** — a famous choir that performs at major festivals
- **Emberforge Operas** — dramatic performances combining music, smithing demonstrations, and fire effects
- **Weaveheart Illuminations** — magical light shows and illusions performed by mages#
#
## Literature
- **Epic poems** recounting the Abominable End and the founding of the Last Stand
- **Practical manuals** — farming guides, smithing techniques, survival handbooks
- **Scouting journals** — published accounts of frontier exploration, wildly popular
- **Religious texts** — holy scriptures of each god, constantly debated by theologians#
#
## Games & Pastimes
- **Strategy games** — simulating military campaigns and monster defense
- **Riddle contests** — popular in Weaveheart's academies
- **Smithing competitions** — Emberforge hosts annual trials of craft
- **Archery tournaments** — Skywatch's signature sport
#
## Attitudes Toward Death & The FrontierThe constant proximity to death and danger has shaped a culture that:
- Celebrates life intensely — festivals are grand, food is plentiful, joy is embraced
- Honors the dead through **memory shrines** — small alcoves in homes where candles are lit for fallen loved ones
- Treats the frontier with a mix of fear and opportunity — it is dangerous, but also where fortunes are made, land is claimed, and glory is found
- Respects adventurers as a necessary and heroic class — they do the work that keeps the monsters at bay and recover the treasures that fuel the economy---
## Adventurers in SocietyAdventurers are not mercenaries for hire — they are **guardians, cleansers, and reclaimers**. Their role in society is akin to an external police force: they handle the threats that lie beyond the walls, clear the ruins that soldiers cannot be spared for, and recover the artifacts and treasures that fuel the economy. The profession carries immense honor and respect.
#
## The Adventurers' Guild — Drakh Ix'tharA continent-wide guild headquartered in the old capital at the center of the continent, with chapter houses in every major settlement and many minor ones. The guild organizes, coordinates, and supports all adventuring activity across the reconquered territories. Its members are collectively known as **Ix'thari** (singular: Ix'thari).**Role of the Guild:**
- **Contract broker** — connects parties with settlements needing monster extermination, ruin clearance, or frontier scouting
- **Licensing & certification** — ensures minimum competence and accountability; a licensed party is recognized anywhere
- **Information network** — shares intelligence about frontier conditions, monster movements, and dangerous sites
- **Support system** — provides healing, equipment repair, safe lodging, and resupply to members in the field
#
## Guild RanksAdventurers advance through recognized ranks based on successful contracts and demonstrable contribution to the reconquering. Ranks are to be defined in Draconic, named after legendary beasts spanning from weakest to strongest, with the highest rank being **Drah Ix'thari** (Dragon Hunter).
#
## Economic RoleAdventurers are vital to the reconquering economy:
- **Clearing monster nests** — making land safe for settlement and resource extraction
- **Recovering treasure** — gold, magic items, and artifacts from monster-occupied ruins
- **Intelligence gathering** — frontier conditions and monster movements that no other scout can reach
- **Field testing** — Emberforge often provides prototype weapons to experienced parties for real combat evaluation---
